report.summary: Three of the four failures come from one product bug: book_dict in app/main.py:143-144 returns the year under the key "published" while create and update return "year", so GET responses and the UI Year column (books.html:19 reads b.year) come out wrong. Fix that first; it accounts for test_created_book_can_be_fetched, test_book_can_be_updated and the UI test. test_current_year_is_accepted is a separate test bug: it posts next year, which the app correctly rejects and which test_invalid_book_is_rejected also asserts.

causes.title: API and UI return the book year under 'published' on reads but 'year' on writes
causes.explanation: book_dict() maps the year column to the key "published" (app/main.py:144). insert_book and api_update_book return the request model via model_dump(), which uses "year". So POST /api/books and PUT /api/books/{id} return {"year": ...} while GET /api/books/{id} and GET /api/books return {"published": ...}. The response shape depends on the endpoint, so a client cannot rely on one schema. The UI has the same mismatch: render_books passes list_books() output, which has no "year" key, to books.html, which renders {{ b.year or "" }} (books.html:19). The Year cell is therefore always blank, so the row never contains '1965'. This is deterministic, not timing-related.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:17: assert fetched.json() == book  -> left has 'published': 1965, right has 'year': 1965
tests/api/test_books_api.py:26-28: expected {"year": 2001} from GET after PUT, actual has 'published': 2001
app/main.py:144: return {"id": row["id"], "title": row["title"], "author": row["author"], "published": row["year"]}
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:16: expect(books.row(title)).to_contain_text("1965") fails; actual row text is 'Dune-7d9786a3 / Frank Herbert / (empty) / Delete'
causes.suggested_fix: Make book_dict emit "year" (not "published") so reads match writes and the template's b.year works. If "published" is an intended public field name, rename the create/update responses and the template and tests to match instead. Pick one shape and apply it everywhere.

causes.title: test_current_year_is_accepted posts next year's date, which the validator correctly rejects
causes.explanation: The test is named 'current year is accepted' but sends year=THIS_YEAR + 1. validate_book rejects any year above date.today().year (app/main.py:83-84), so the API correctly returns 422. The same file's parametrized test_invalid_book_is_rejected asserts that THIS_YEAR + 1 must be rejected, so the two tests contradict each other. The app behaves as designed. The test should send THIS_YEAR, which is the boundary the validator accepts. This is deterministic: it fails on every run, and the failure is a date-independent logic error.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:47-50: response = api.create_book(title=unique("New"), author="Someone", year=THIS_YEAR + 1); assert response.status_code == 201
app/main.py:83-84: if not 1 <= book.year <= this_year: raise HTTPException(422, ...)
causes.suggested_fix: Change line 48 to use year=THIS_YEAR so the test checks the current-year boundary it is named for. Keep THIS_YEAR + 1 in test_invalid_book_is_rejected. Optionally assert that the 201 response body contains the year.
